summary.intent: Debug why the FUSE-mounted folder shows stale file content after editing a file in the web UI and saving it.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified in `crates/fuse/src/inode.rs` — `populate_folder()` never re-resolved already-resolved inodes even when `modified_at` changed. Fix applied, tested (37 tests pass), pushed to `fix/fuse-stale-file-after-web-edit`, and PR #454 created.

repo: FUSE metadata cache has a 30s TTL; `drain_refresh_completions` calls `populate_folder` after each TTL expiry.
Content cache is keyed by CID (content-addressed), so it correctly serves different data for different CIDs — the stale CID reference was the actual bug, not the content cache.
File IPNS private key and encrypted key hex are stable across edits; only the CID changes when file content is updated.
The project uses a gsd-debugger subagent workflow with debug session files stored in `.planning/debug/*.md`.

code.finding: `populate_folder()` preserved existing `InodeKind` wholesale for `file_meta_resolved: true` files, never comparing incoming `modified_at` against existing inode `mtime`. Fixed to reset resolved state when `modified_at` is newer, triggering fresh IPNS resolution on the next drain cycle.

workflow: Spurious `Cargo.lock` changes (no corresponding `Cargo.toml` bump) should be reverted before committing to avoid noise in PRs.
The gsd-debugger subagent pattern isolates investigation context (file reads, hypothesis testing) from the main orchestrator context, keeping the main session lean.
Debug session files in `.planning/debug/` are committed to the repo as part of the fix workflow for traceability.

friction: Cargo.lock picked up a phantom version bump for `cipherbox-fuse` with no Cargo.toml change, requiring a manual revert before committing.
open_items: Manual end-to-end verification still pending: user needs to build the desktop app, run the upload→edit→wait→check flow, and confirm the fix resolves the stale content issue in practice.
The 30-60s wait time for the metadata TTL cycle may be worth tuning if faster propagation is desired after web UI saves.
